title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 50 is the end of the bracketed duality remark and the start of a new paragraph in the letter to Deligne dated 10.12.1965.

(1) End of the duality remark. The previous page sketches a generalisation of the relative duality theorem f_! ⊣ f^! (later SGA 4 XVIII). It applies to a smooth compactifiable f : (X,B) → (Y,A) of ringed sites, where A is any sheaf of rings killed by an integer n prime to the residue characteristics. The definition is f^!K = RHom_{f^{-1}A}(B, f^{-1}K ⊗ T_{X/Y}[2d]). The proof splits into the case f^{-1}A ≅ B and the case f = id. Grothendieck doubts that this follows formally from the case A = Z/nZ. He makes the same remark for global duality, which should be stated for general sheaves of rings and not only the constant Z/nZ.

(2) The main new paragraph: a conjectural p-adic analogue of the complex comparison. Over C one has H^*(X^an, Z) ⊗ C ≅ H_dR(X), and H^*(X^an, Z) ⊗ Z_ℓ ≅ H_et(X, Z_ℓ). Grothendieck asks for an analogue over K, an algebraically closed complete non-archimedean field of characteristic 0 with residue characteristic p (e.g. C_p). There should be a Z_p-linear map H^*(X_et, Z_p) → H_dR^*(X/K) inducing H_et ⊗_{Z_p} K ≅ H_dR.

Proposed construction:
- Pass to Tate's rigid-analytic space X^an. He notes this is a site (a G-topology), not a topological space, which explains Tate's initial difficulties.
- Hope that for torsion sheaves H(X_et) = H(X^an).
- Hope, "by an excess of optimism", that H(X^an, Z_p) = lim H(X^an, Z/p^n), and hence equals H(X_et, Z_p).
- Use Z_p ⊂ K = constant functions on X^an to map H(X^an, Z_p) → H(X^an, K) → H_dR(X^an).
- Identify H_dR(X^an) = H_dR(X) by rigid GAGA.
- The key input, on the next page, is a rigid Poincaré lemma: the de Rham complex resolves the constant sheaf K.

On the next page Grothendieck himself doubts all this. He recalls Tate saying that constant-coefficient rigid cohomology already gives wrong Betti numbers for H^1 of elliptic curves. He then turns to the characteristic p map H^*(X, F_p) → H^*(X, O_X) → H_dR via Frobenius and Cartier.

The problem served is to find a p-adic de Rham comparison: the seed of the 'mysterious functor' (ICM 1970) and of Fontaine–Messing / Faltings / Scholze p-adic Hodge theory.
errors: Over a complete algebraically closed K, the cohomology of the rigid G-site with constant coefficients does not agree with étale cohomology, even for torsion coefficients. For an elliptic curve with good reduction, H^1(X^an, Z/p) is 0, while H^1_et has rank 2. One needs the étale site of the rigid space (later Berkovich and Huber), not the rigid G-topology. Grothendieck half-recognises this on the next page via Tate's remark.

The rigid Poincaré lemma fails for the G-topology. On an affinoid disc, closed 1-forms need not be exact: antiderivatives of convergent series need not converge, because of the 1/n factors. So H(X^an, K_const) is not de Rham cohomology. The constant-sheaf cohomology resembles the topological cohomology of the reduction graph (e.g. the Tate curve gives rank 1 for H^1).

There is no Z_p-linear (Galois-compatible) map H_et ⊗ K → H_dR that is an isomorphism compatible with the natural structures. A period ring such as B_dR (Fontaine) is required; Tate's 1967 Hodge–Tate decomposition already shows the C_p(i)-twists. An abstract K-isomorphism exists only for dimension reasons.
Equality of lim H(X^an, Z/p^n) with H(X^an, Z_p) needs Mittag-Leffler-type control. This is part of the 'excess of optimism', which is not justified.

ideas.what: Duality theorem f^! for smooth compactifiable morphisms of ringed sites with general torsion coefficient rings A (n invertible), f^!K = RHom_{f^{-1}A}(B, f^{-1}K ⊗ T[2d])
ideas.modern_name: Relative Poincaré/Verdier duality in étale cohomology with general torsion coefficient rings (SGA 4 XVIII)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, SGA 4 Exp. XVIII (1973), on Grothendieck's program
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 XVIII (Deligne's write-up) treats general torsion rings; how much of this ringed-site generality appears there: unsure

ideas.what: Conjectural Z_p-linear comparison map H^*(X_et, Z_p) → H_dR(X/K) for X over an algebraically closed complete p-adic field, as an analogue of the Betti–de Rham comparison over C
ideas.modern_name: p-adic comparison theorem / 'mysterious functor' (de Rham comparison, B_dR)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ICM Nice 1970, 'mysterious functor'); Tate 1967 (Hodge–Tate); Fontaine 1979–82 (conjectures C_dR, C_cris); Faltings, Fontaine–Messing, Tsuji (proofs)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux', Actes ICM Nice 1970 (mysterious functor); this 1965 formulation is in an unpublished letter

ideas.what: Strategy: go through Tate's rigid-analytic space and prove a rigid Poincaré lemma, so that the de Rham complex resolves the constant sheaf; then compare H(X^an, Z_p) with H(X_et, Z_p) and use rigid GAGA
ideas.modern_name: Rigid/adic analytic comparison plus a Poincaré lemma for period sheaves (OB_dR on the pro-étale site)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scholze 2013 ('p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties'); Faltings (almost étale); Berkovich/Huber for étale comparison of torsion cohomology

ideas.what: Remark that Tate's rigid spaces form a site (Grothendieck/G-topology) not definable by an ordinary topology
ideas.modern_name: G-topology / Grothendieck topology on rigid spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate 1962/1971; Kiehl; Grothendieck's notion of site

ideas.what: Rigid-analytic GAGA for de Rham cohomology of proper X

missed.claim: A dated (10.12.1965) explicit conjecture that p-adic étale cohomology of varieties over an algebraically closed complete p-adic field should map Z_p-linearly into de Rham cohomology and become isomorphic after ⊗K. This predates Tate's 1966 Driebergen Hodge–Tate paper and Grothendieck's 1970 'mysterious functor'. It is an early documented origin of p-adic Hodge theory's comparison problem.
missed.quote: savoir que H^*(X,Z_p) doit s'envoyer alors de façon Z_p-linéaire dans la cohomologie de De-Rham H^*(X), qui serait isomorphe alors à H^*(X,Z_p)⊗_{Z_p} K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to the history of p-adic Hodge theory. It shows Grothendieck posed the étale–de Rham comparison over C_p already in 1965, in the same letter as crystalline ideas.

missed.claim: The proposed mechanism — go to the rigid-analytic site, prove a Poincaré lemma there, and compare constant-coefficient cohomology with étale cohomology — is essentially the architecture of Scholze's 2013 proof. That proof uses the pro-étale site of the adic space, the Poincaré lemma for OB_dR, and the primitive comparison theorem. Grothendieck foresaw the shape, and also why naive constant coefficients on the G-topology fail.
missed.quote: L' "excès" plus haut serait justifié essentiellement par un "lemme de Poincaré" rigide-analytique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, Scholze's route is a vindication of this 1965 heuristic once the site and coefficient sheaf are corrected. This is worth recording in histories of the subject.

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags a question about duality: whether duality with an arbitrary torsion sheaf of rings A on Y (and B on X) follows formally from the case A = Z/nZ. He suspects not, and suggests including the general form in SGA 4.
missed.quote: Je n'ai pas regardé si par hasard il pourrait se déduire du cas particulier A=(Z/nZ)_Y comme simple corollaire, mais ça m'étonnerait.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Duality for general coefficient rings is now standard (e.g. via ∞-categorical six-functor formalisms), so this is likely settled in spirit.

deep.surprise_reason: The duality material is routine. The p-adic paragraph is a notable early (1965) explicit formulation of the étale–de Rham comparison over C_p, with a rigid-analytic Poincaré-lemma strategy that anticipates Scholze's approach. Grothendieck's later 'mysterious functor' and his general interest are known, so the idea itself is not new; the value is the early date and the specific strategy.
transcription_corrections: In 'théorème de dualité [-x-]globale', the struck character is overtyped on the g of 'globale'; read 'dualité globale'.
The handwritten insertion 'alg clos ,' sits above 'valué', so the phrase reads 'corps de base est alg clos, valué complet non archimédien'.
The handwritten 'K' is inserted after 'corps des fractions'.
'De-Rham' and 'De Rham' both appear (typed 'De#Rham' with an overstrike in one place).
